name: Emery Colón
life: “I still remember paying for day-old bread out of a birthday envelope.” Wednesday often includes a stop at Paper & Pine Books, where Emery starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I caught a bus across town for the cheap day-old bread. Both applicants asked me what should stay cheap.
appearance: Emery has a high puff tied with plain cord, fine brows over wide-set eyes, and a favorite piece of clothing, a red windbreaker. It usually goes with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. When somebody else has the floor, Emery gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in.
personality: Emery is firm about boundaries and unusually forgiving of somebody who admits to crossing one. Demands to act grateful for unwanted help can end a friendship.
agenda: To protect an affordable day-old loaf.
family: Jacqueline Glass is Emery’s half-sibling. Emery calls about good news first. Jacqueline is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *An empty dedication*, Jacqueline says, “I edited the manuscript so heavily I was beginning to hear my own voice.”
connections: Tara Dean. Sponsor and bread customer both care whether the new job leaves a loaf ordinary workers can buy.

reactions.situation: The new baker gets the first oven slot
reactions.response: Emery makes sure the other applicant gets a comparable chance with the same oven.

reactions.situation: A traveler asks for the last seat at the bus stop
reactions.response: Emery asks the person already using it whether they can comfortably stand, rather than presuming who needs it most.

reactions.situation: If a relative arrives with a solution nobody requested
reactions.response: Emery thanks them for coming and explains the part that still belongs to the household.
